Check Q3: 0.9995×0.999×0.9995×0.995 = compute: 0.9995×0.999=0.9985005; ×0.9995=0.9980010; ×0.995=0.99301... = 0.9930100. So 99.30% correct. Downtime 0.00699×720=5.0328 → 5.0 h correct. (c) 0.999975 → 99.9975% — but requirement says two decimal places percentages; 99.9975% is more precise; downtime 0.018 h → 0.0 h to one decimal. Minor precision issue. Also (c) end-to-end: 0.9985005×0.9995×0.999975 = 0.9974765... ≈ 99.75%, not 99.9975%! Student only reported payment availability, not end-to-end. Actually student says "new availability of placing an order is 99.9975%" — that's wrong; end-to-end = 0.99301 with payment replaced: 0.9985005×0.9995×0.999975 = 0.9974765 → 99.75%. So part (c) end-to-end incorrect. Downtime 0.0025235×720=1.82 h, not 0.018. So C3: one part incorrect → Proficient, 5-6. Give 5 or 6. Method correct, one part incorrect → 6? "one arithmetic or rounding slip, or exactly one part is incorrect" — Proficient. Give 6.

Q1: availability response measure "stay up most of the time" not measurable → Proficient, 4.

Q2: excellent, two scenario-specific trade-offs, downside acknowledged → 5-6. Give 6? Trade-offs specific, downside acknowledged. 6.

Q4: circuit breaker, mechanism, applied, drawback? No drawback/tuning consideration given explicitly — threshold example given but no drawback. Proficient → 4.

Q5: CAP used incorrectly ("choose consistency and availability, give up partition tolerance" — partitions can't be given up). Techniques: Redis cache, idempotency key. Proficient → 4.

Q6: no negative consequence → Proficient → 4.

C7: word limits? Q2 seems >150 words (~200). Q4 ~160. References cited IEEE. Proficient → 3.
